title: Sequence-aware version pinning and routing compatibility policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and implement a practical policy and tooling for version pinning and routing compatibility that accounts for model/runtime pairings, sequence-length and KV-cache semantics, and graceful fallback behavior across runtime and model upgrades.

Background: As we expand LTS channels and roll out faster runtime feature releases, many customers pin to combinations of model and runtime versions. In the field we observed two classes of failures: (1) silent correctness regressions caused by inference kernel/quantization changes when a model is served on a newer runtime, and (2) high-latency or OOM errors when runtime memory layout or KV cache semantics change mid-rollout. Existing routing only matches on model family and semantic version; it doesn’t encode sequence-length expectations, KV-cache compatibility, or optional feature flags (e.g., rotary embeddings vs ALiBi support).

Scope: This ticket covers the policy (rules), compatibility metadata model, and first-pass enforcement/rollout tooling for hosted and Dedicated modes. Private deployments will receive a compatibility manifest and migration checklist as part of runtime-2.0 documentation (separate doc).
acceptance_criteria:
- Compatibility metadata format specified and documented (fields: runtime_semver, model_schema_hash, kv_cache_semantics, expected_max_seq, optional_features list).
- Router evaluates compatibility during routing decisions and emits compatibility_score and failure_reason in tracing for every routed request.
- Soft-pin behavior implemented: default routes attempt target pinned pair; on observed compatibility failures (OOM, correctness alerts) automatic fallback to a compatible runtime/model variant occurs per policy.
- E2E tests that simulate mismatch classes (kernel mismatch, quantization mismatch, KV cache migration) and verify fallback and tracing contain root cause.
- Migration playbook added to runtime-2.0 release notes for Dedicated and Private customers.
implementation_notes:
Design choices:
1) Use a compact compatibility manifest published to model catalog per model-version and to runtime image metadata per runtime build. Both manifests are simple JSON key/values and include a manifest_hash to detect drift.
2) Router decision algorithm computes a compatibility_score (0-100) from strict checks (schema hash match, kv_semantics equal) and soft checks (optional_features superset). Score threshold configurable by customer tiers.
3) Introduce a runtime feature gate 'compatibility-strict-mode' for internal canary traffic to catch regressions early.
4) Fallback mechanics: when a pinned route fails at runtime with high-severity error, increment a per-tenant incident counter. After N failures within T minutes, the routing layer temporarily routes new requests to the highest-scoring compatible variant and triggers alerts and rollback suggestions.
5) For model versions with large sequence-length regressions, the router annotates requests with "seq_hint" and prefers runtimes with proven long-seq kernel support.

Trade-offs considered: strict enforcement prevents accidental regressions but increases churn for small internal runtime changes (more releases marked incompatible). We adopt configurable strictness per customer and default to soft-pin for self-serve customers to minimize disruptions.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (internal canary, 2 weeks): enable compatibility-strict-mode for 5% of internal requests; collect traces and compatibility_score metrics.
Phase 2 (early customers, 4 weeks): opt-in list of Dedicated customers who opted for stricter guarantees; provide migration playbook and run compatibility scanner against their pinned pairs.
Phase 3 (general availability, runtime-2.0): default router emits warnings but performs soft fallback; enterprise tier can enable automatic hard-isolation where incompatible model/runtime pairings are rejected.
Phase 4 (post-GA): add automated migration jobs and a 'compatibility-scan' CI check for model onboarding pipeline.
test_plan:
- Unit tests: compatibility manifest parsing, manifest_hash verification.
- Integration tests: router decision matrix with synthetic manifests covering permutations of kv_semantics, optional features, max_seq.
- Chaos tests: inject OOM and tokenization-drift errors to verify automatic fallback triggers and that fallbacks do not create request storms.
- Regression harness: run saved prompt suite against model pinned to old runtime vs same model on new runtime to detect output drift; attach diff thresholds to alerting.
- Load test: ensure extra routing checks add <1% CPU overhead at 99th percentile under production QPS.
